mainTopic: Whether the principle of פי תקרה יורד וסותם (the roof's edge 'descends and seals' as a wall) applies to a סוכה built on top of an אכסדרה (portico) without side posts, and whether the מחלוקת between אביי and רבא matches the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל.
overview: This amud picks up in the middle of אביי's ruling about a סוכה built on a portico that has no side posts. אביי says it is כשרה because of פי תקרה יורד וסותם: the edge of the roof counts as a wall that 'comes down and closes' the open side. רבא says it is פסולה because we do not use that idea. רבא challenges אביי: by your logic, even a סוכה with its middle wall removed, leaving two facing walls, should be כשרה. אביי concedes that one case, because it is like a מבוי המפולש, a passage open at both ends. The גמרא then suggests that אביי and רבא are simply repeating the older מחלוקת of רב and שמואל. That dispute is about carrying on שבת in a portico standing in a field. רב allows carrying throughout the portico because he applies פי תקרה. שמואל allows carrying only within four אמות because he does not. The גמרא rejects the comparison: according to שמואל, everyone would agree.

steps.title: אביי's reasoning: the roof's edge acts as a wall
steps.stepSummary: אביי's reason for calling the סוכה כשרה: we apply פי תקרה יורד וסותם.
steps.simpleTranslation: [אביי said it is fit], because we say that the edge of the roof comes down and closes off the opening.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of אביי's statement. Here he gives his reason why a סוכה on a portico with no side posts is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The portico has no proper walls on its open side. אביי uses a legal idea: the edge of the roof is treated as if it extends straight down and forms a wall. That imagined wall makes up for the missing one.

keyTerms.meaning: The edge (literally 'mouth') of the roof or ceiling
Descends and seals, as if forming a wall
We say / we apply (this principle)

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody claims there is a physical wall here. פי תקרה יורד וסותם is a legal idea: the הלכה treats the roof's edge as though it were a wall.

phrases.english: we say that the edge of the roof
phrases.notes: This continues אביי's words from the lines before: 'אביי said it is fit, because…'

phrases.english: descends and seals (the opening).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's ruling, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the סוכה is כשרה because פי תקרה יורד וסותם.

steps.title: רבא rules the סוכה unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees: the סוכה is פסולה because we do not apply פי תקרה יורד וסותם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is unfit, because we do not say that the edge of the roof comes down and closes off the opening.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite ruling. He says the סוכה is פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא rejects the imagined wall completely. Without it, the open side stays open, so the סוכה lacks enough walls.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit / invalid
We do not say / do not apply

phrases.english: Rava said: It is unfit —
we do not say that the edge of the roof
descends and seals.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא: the סוכה is פסולה because we do not apply פי תקרה יורד וסותם.

steps.title: רבא challenges אביי: then even a סוכה missing its middle wall should be valid
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that אביי's principle would make even a סוכה with only two parallel walls כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to אביי: According to you, who say the roof's edge comes down and seals, then even if someone removed the middle wall, [the סוכה should still be fit]!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's idea by pushing it to an extreme case that seems clearly wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a סוכה with two walls facing each other and the wall connecting them removed. If roof edges really count as walls, they would 'close' both open sides, and the סוכה would be כשרה. רבא assumes that result is unacceptable, so the principle itself must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you / by your logic
He removed / reduced
The middle wall (the one connecting two parallel walls)

phrases.english: Rava said to Abaye:
according to you, who said
the edge of the roof descends and seals,
[then the sukkah should be fit] even if he removed the middle wall!
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't say it outright, but that would be a ridiculous result.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אַבָּיֵי, לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's use of פי תקרה יורד וסותם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio: if the principle is true, a סוכה with only two parallel walls would be כשרה, which seems unacceptable.

steps.title: אביי concedes that case: it is like an open-ended alley
steps.stepSummary: אביי agrees the two-parallel-walls case is פסולה, because it resembles a מבוי המפולש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I agree with you in that case, because it is like an alley that is open at both ends.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by agreeing with רבא about that one case. He explains why it is different from his own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the two open sides face each other, the space is a straight passageway open at both ends, like a מבוי המפולש. In that shape the imagined roof-edge wall does not work. In the ordinary portico case, the principle still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: I concede to you / I agree with you
In that (case)
An alleyway open at both ends (a through-passage)

phrases.english: He said to him: I concede to you in that case,
because it is like an alleyway open at both ends.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: concede the extreme case and limit the principle so it does not reach it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The principle seemed to apply equally to every roof edge, including two facing open sides.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the space is open on two opposite sides like a מבוי המפולש, the principle does not work. Otherwise it does.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי keeps his principle but limits it: it does not help when the space becomes a through-passage open at both ends.

steps.title: Is this the same dispute as רב and שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אביי and רבא are simply repeating the older מחלוקת of רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that אביי and רבא disagree about the same issue that רב and שמואל disagreed about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a comparison. It suggests that this argument already exists between earlier אמוראים, and the next step brings that earlier argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase לימא signals a tentative proposal, not a conclusion. If the comparison holds, אביי follows רב and רבא follows שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a tentative suggestion)
In the dispute of
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: לימא usually introduces a suggestion that the גמרא ends up rejecting. Do not treat it as the final answer.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Abaye and Rava
disagree in the dispute of Rav and Shmuel?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the internal debate to asking whether it matches an earlier מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the אביי and רבא dispute is the same as the רב and שמואל dispute.

steps.title: The רב and שמואל dispute about a portico in a field
steps.stepSummary: רב allows carrying throughout a portico in a field because of פי תקרה. שמואל allows only four אמות because he rejects it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: About a portico standing in a field, רב said one may carry throughout all of it, because we say the roof's edge comes down and seals. שמואל said one may carry in it only within four אמות, because we do not say the roof's edge comes down and seals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the earlier מחלוקת so we can compare it to אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a roofed portico without real walls, standing in an open field (a כרמלית). If the roof edges count as walls, the portico becomes a רשות היחיד, and carrying anywhere inside is allowed, as רב says. If they do not count, it stays like the field, where carrying is limited to four אמות, as שמואל says.

keyTerms.meaning: A portico, a roofed structure without full walls
An open field (a כרמלית for שבת)
To move or carry objects (on שבת)
Four cubits, the limited carrying distance

steps.whyThisMatters: The same principle governs both שבת domains and סוכה walls. That is why the גמרא can try to link the two disputes.

phrases.english: As it was stated: A portico in a field,
Rav said: It is permitted to carry throughout all of it,
because we say the edge of the roof descends and seals.
And Shmuel said: One may not carry in it
except within four cubits,
because we do not say the edge of the roof
descends and seals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the comparison proposed in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: carrying is allowed throughout the portico (פי תקרה applies). שמואל: only four אמות (פי תקרה does not apply).

steps.title: Rejection: according to שמואל, אביי and רבא would agree
steps.stepSummary: The comparison fails. Under שמואל's view, both אביי and רבא would agree the principle does not apply to a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 5. The disputes do not line up neatly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not use the roof-edge principle even for carrying on שבת. So no one following שמואל could use it to make a סוכה כשרה, and אביי could not hold like שמואל. The real argument between אביי and רבא must therefore exist only within רב's view, which the גמרא is about to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: According to (the view of)
Everyone
They do not disagree

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת of אביי and רבא is not simply רב versus שמואל. Under שמואל, both agree the סוכה is not saved by the roof's edge.

phrases.english: According to Shmuel,
everyone agrees (no one disagrees).

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed match between the two disputes.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that אביי = רב and רבא = שמואל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under שמואל no one applies פי תקרה here, so אביי cannot follow שמואל. The dispute must exist only within רב's view.
